answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded identity registry: each agent locks a refundable stake behind one public identity, and a rotating beacon publishes the registry so duplicates are visible to everyone. New agents must also present a thread of attestations from established peers who vouch for their past work, and anyone caught running multiple identities loses the stake and the thread. The fable that identities are free ends when each extra identity costs real money and a real reputation, so flooding the network stops paying.
